Info Edge (India) Limited has informed the Exchange that Notice is hereby given that the following resolutions are proposed to be passed through Postal Ballot in accordance with the provisions of Section 372A and other applicable provisions, if any, of the Companies Act, 1956 (the "Act") read with Section 192A of the Act and the rules made there under. The Company proposes the same for the approval of its Members through Postal Ballot. (1) Special Resolution for increasing FII investment limit upto 40% under Portfolio Investment Scheme. (2) Special Resolution under Section 81 (1A) of the Companies Act 1956, for further issue of capital. (3) Ordinary Resolution under Section 293 (1) (d) of the Companies Act, 1956, for increasing the borrowing limit of the company. (4) Special Resolution under Section 372A of the Companies Act, 1956, for increasing the investment limit of the Company. The Board of Directors has appointed Mr.N.C. Khanna, Company Secretary in Practice, as the Scrutinizer for conducting the voting through Postal Ballot in a fair and transparent manner. The duly completed postal ballot form should reach the Scrutinizer on or before the close of working hours on January 22, 2008. Either Mr. Sanjeev Bikhchandani, Managing Director or Mr. Hitesh Oberoi, Director or Mr.Ambarish Raghuvanshi, Director of the Company shall announce the result of the postal ballot on January 23, 2008. A copy of the Notice of the Postal Ballot shall be available on the NSE website (http://www.nseindia.com) under: Corporates > Latest Announcements and on the Extranet Server (/Common/Corporate Announcements). For more details click here.

Info Edge (India) Limited has informed the Exchange that the Board of Directors in their meeting held on December 21, 2007 approved and decided to recommend the following matters for approval of the Shareholders through Postal Ballot: (1) Increase Foreign Institutional Investment (FII) limit upto 40% of the paid-up capital under Portfolio Investment Scheme from the current 24%; (2) Resolution under Section 81 (1A) of the Companies Act, 1956 to raise further capital upto an aggregate amount of Rs. 500 cores (including share premium) by different alternative available mechanism under applicable laws like QIPs, GDR, FCCB, ADR etc.; (3) Resolution under Section 293 (1) (d) of the Companies Act, 1956 to raise borrowing limits upto an aggregate amount of Rs. 500 crores; (4) Resolution under Section 372A of the Companies Act, 1956 to increase the investment limit by Rs. 300 crores over and above the statutory limit under Section-372A of the Companies Act, 1956.
